raw_case_text:
A 22-year-old Malay female without chronic systemic comorbidity presented with left eye floaters for 2 weeks. Later, she developed left eye temporal visual field defect and metamorphopsia for 3 days. However, there was no eye pain or eye redness. Further history revealed that she has a hedgehog and a guinea pig at home, but denied being bitten or scratched by them. She also denied any history of fever, recent traveling, sexual promiscuity, and oral intake of any uncooked food. Her visual acuity at presentation was 6/12 in the left eye and 6/6 in the right eye. Left eye relative afferent pupillary defect was barely positive with mild anterior chamber reaction. Intraocular pressure was normal in both eyes (right eye: 16 mmHg and left eye: 17 mmHg). Fundus examination of the left eye showed mild vitritis, swollen optic disc with macular star, crops of active choroidal lesions at superonasal retina with a linear arrangement in the form of migratory track nasally (Figure 1). However, there were no nematodes seen on fundus examination. Optical coherence tomography of the left eye showed minimal subretinal fluid at the macula with some hyperreflectivity lesions (Figure 2). Optic nerve examination showed red desaturation with reduced contrast sensitivity and impaired color vision in the left eye as compared with the right eye. Humphrey visual field on the left eye showed superior temporal field defect with enlargement of blind spot. Right eye examination was otherwise unremarkable. Her systemic examination was normal. There was no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly.
On the basis of the clinical findings with the presence of crops of choroidal lesions with migratory track, she was treated as for presumed DUSN. Focal argon laser was given to the area of migratory track followed by oral albendazole 400 mg 12 hourly for 6 weeks. Her left eye vision improved from 6/12 to 6/6 at 1 week after treatment. Fundus showed resolution of vitritis, regression of optic disc swelling as well as resolution of crops of choroidal lesions, with no new active lesion (Figure 3). Repeat optical coherence tomography of the left eye showed resolution of subretinal fluid at the macula (Figure 4).
Blood investigation was done to rule out other infective causes. Her investigations showed normal full blood count with no eosinophilia, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) was 33 mm per hour. Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) serology for Burkholderia pseudomallei and Leptospira was negative. A chest radiograph was normal and Mantoux test was negative. However, immunoglobulin (Ig) M serology for Bartonella henselae was positive (titer 1:48). Based on the positive serological test, a second diagnosis of bartonellosis or CSD was made. Oral doxycycline 100 mg 12 hourly for 4 weeks was added after 2 weeks of administration of oral albendazole. Follow-up at 1 month after completion of both albendazole and doxycycline therapy showed that left eye vision acuity was stable at 6/6. Fundus showed complete resolution of choroidal lesions and resolution of neuroretinitis (Figure 5). Written informed consent was obtained from the patient for the publication of the paper and the photographs. This case report was approved by the Ethics Committee of Hospital Selayang.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 22-year-old Malay woman presented with a 2-week history of left eye floaters and a 3-day history of left temporal visual field defect and metamorphopsia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with painless left eye floaters for 2 weeks, followed over the preceding 3 days by a left temporal visual field defect and visual distortion (metamorphopsia) without ocular redness or pain.
subjective.past_medical_history: No chronic systemic comorbidities. Kept a pet hedgehog and guinea pig at home but denied animal bites or scratches, recent travel, uncooked food consumption, or high-risk sexual behavior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for left eye floaters, temporal visual field loss, and metamorphopsia; negative for ocular pain, redness, or fever.

objective.physical_examination: Presenting visual acuity was 6/12 in the left eye and 6/6 in the right eye, with normal intraocular pressures (16 mmHg OD, 17 mmHg OS). Left eye examination revealed a trace relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD), red color desaturation, reduced contrast sensitivity, impaired color vision, mild anterior chamber cellular reaction, mild vitritis, optic disc edema with a macular star (neuroretinitis), and crops of active superonasal choroidal lesions arranged linearly along a nasal migratory track (no visible subretinal nematode). Right eye exam and systemic physical exam (no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly) were normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Full blood count was normal without eosinophilia; ESR was 33 mm/h. VDRL, Mantoux tuberculin skin test, chest radiograph, and serologies for Burkholderia pseudomallei and Leptospira were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Left eye spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrated minimal macular subretinal fluid with hyperreflective lesions; Humphrey visual field testing showed a left superior temporal field defect with blind spot enlargement. Serum Bartonella henselae IgM serology was positive at a titer of 1:48.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with left eye neuroretinitis and multifocal choroiditis due to serologically confirmed Bartonella henselae infection (cat-scratch disease / bartonellosis, IgM titer 1:48) and presumed diffuse unilateral subacute neuroretinitis (DUSN); leptospirosis, melioidosis, syphilis, and tuberculosis were excluded. Treated initially with focal argon laser photocoagulation over the migratory choroidal track and oral albendazole (400 mg q12h for 6 weeks), with addition of oral doxycycline (100 mg q12h for 4 weeks) after positive Bartonella serology. Left visual acuity recovered to 6/6 within 1 week and remained 6/6 with complete resolution of neuroretinitis, subretinal fluid, and choroidal lesions at 1-month post-treatment follow-up.
